name: What is the difference between single-pane, double-pane, and triple-pane windows?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between single-pane, double-pane, and triple-pane windows?

acceptedAnswer.text: The primary difference lies in the number of glass panes and their insulating properties. Single-pane windows have only one layer of glass, offering minimal insulation and poor energy efficiency. Double-pane windows feature two panes of glass separated by a sealed air or gas-filled space, significantly improving insulation and reducing heat transfer. Triple-pane windows add a third pane and another sealed space, providing the highest level of energy efficiency, noise reduction, and often superior condensation resistance.
acceptedAnswer.description: Single-pane has one glass layer; double-pane has two with a sealed space; triple-pane has three for maximum insulation.
